extracted.intended_audience: corporate communicators, communication professionals, member companies, academics and institutions interested in business/corporate communication (primarily Brazil, with international reach)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational principles and programmatic pillars guiding best practices, professional development, research, publication, and event programming in corporate/business communication. This is a values-and-pillar framework for institutions and practitioners to align strategy, ethics, and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: produce knowledge and share best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of Aberje is to produce knowledge and share best practices in order to strengthen communication in companies and institutions and reinforce the strategic and civic role of the communicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should prioritize knowledge production and dissemination, and reinforce both the strategic (organizational goals) and civic (social responsibility) functions of communicators. Programs, publications and training should demonstrate how they advance these aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main goal: training and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the role of communication in companies and institutions by training and developing professionals and by creating and disseminating knowledge in business communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate work by its contribution to professional capacity-building: courses, workshops, mentorships, and other training formats should demonstrably develop practitioner skills and competencies in corporate communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision: global think tank aspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Aberje seeks to be a global think tank for Communication and Business Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives and outputs should aim for thought leadership, international engagement, and high-quality research or analysis suitable for global discourse in communication and business relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key principle — Associativism (collaboration and peer learning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniting efforts around a common idea is the foundation of any association; associativism fosters a space for peer interaction among market competitors who also share common practices, beliefs, and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should enable peer exchange, mutual learning, and critical reflection. The association should institutionalize shared ideals via training, research, curation, recognition of best practices, and foster alignment between individual, organizational and societal interests. Avoid inward-looking approaches by engaging broader society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value — Ethics (integrity and civility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics: an ethical person acts in accordance with unwritten norms and principles of good coexistence and regard for others; communication cultivates coexistence, respect, and civility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications and communicators should demonstrate integrity, respect for legal and unwritten norms, and foster civil discourse. Projects and guidance should reflect ethical reflection on corporate values and social impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value — Innovation with memory and sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation: pursue novelty and inventiveness, but engage in dialogue with history and memory, recognize relationships with nature, and frame innovation within sustainability limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative communications should balance originality with institutional memory and consider environmental and social sustainability. Novelty is valued when it is contextualized and responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value — Plurality (diversity as source of richness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plurality: recognize the inherent value of diversity (ethnic, cultural, religious, sexual, ecological, political, generational) and move beyond tolerance toward learning from difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication practices, hiring, content and programming should actively engage diverse perspectives and treat diversity as a resource for learning and improved outcomes, not merely compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value — Humanism (reason, education, preservation of nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanism: promote and defend reason, education, science and the arts; preserve nature and develop conditions necessary for sustainable coexistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should foreground human-centered analysis, support evidence-based practice, education and cultural engagement, and incorporate environmental stewardship into communication strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Content (knowledge production and debate)
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and share knowledge of the area and encourage debate on the key issues in business communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess outputs by their capacity to inform, provoke constructive debate, and synthesize knowledge relevant to practitioners and institutions in business communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Memory and Reference Center (archiving corporate communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first archive dedicated to Corporate Communication in Latin America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize preservation, accessibility, and curation of historical records as resources for research, teaching, and practice; consider archival standards and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Editora Aberje (publishing theoretical and practical books)
rubrics_metrics.description: An editorial label focused on publishing theoretical and practical books in the communication field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications should balance theory and practice, targeting both academic and practitioner audiences; quality editorial standards and relevance to the field are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Aberje Research Center (studies on organizational communication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies on communication within organizations and the professionals in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should examine organizational practices, professional roles and trends; prioritize rigorous methods, relevance to practice, and dissemination to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Revista CE Comunicação Empresarial (semiannual dossier)
rubrics_metrics.description: A semiannual dossier that explores key topics influencing companies and their communication strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial selection should focus on topics of strategic importance to corporate communicators; issues should combine case studies, analysis and practical guidance on communication strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Aberje Portal (digital platform for practitioners)
rubrics_metrics.description: A digital platform with essential content for communication professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online content should be timely, practical, and targeted to practitioners' needs; ensure usability, topical relevance, and regular updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pillar — Aberje Trends (events showcasing cases and debates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brings together hundreds of communicators to showcase, through case presentations, lectures, and debates — focusing on external communication, internal communication, government relations, and ESG — how communication should act as a catalyst for change and solutions in this new era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events should highlight empirical cases, encourage knowledge exchange across domains (external/internal/gov relations/ESG), and emphasize communication's role in driving change and practical solutions.
